headline: Who owns the water: Madurai's allocation ledger
intro: Madurai drinks under one of India's oldest live water instruments: an 1886 lease that sends Periyar water east into the Vaigai, and a 2018 PWD letter granting the city a year-round share of it. This ledger shows what that paper promises, what the city actually draws, and how solid the record is.
unit_note: Madurai's entitlement is stated in its native units - cusecs (continuous release) and mcft/year (annual volume) - alongside MLD equivalents where published. Units are never converted silently.

authorities.name: TN Water Resources Department (PWD)
authorities.role: The state's water department. It operates the dams and canals of the Periyar-Vaigai system - including the Vaigai dam Madurai drinks from - and issues the release orders that decide who gets water, when.
authorities.capacity: Vaigai dam serves irrigation + Madurai + en-route towns
authorities.committed: 51.09 cusecs (125 MLD) continuous to Madurai Corporation
authorities.tension: The system exists first for irrigation: the same releases that fill Madurai's intake serve farm turns, so the city's year-round entitlement is a carve-out that must survive every drought-year negotiation.

arrangements.source: Periyar-Vaigai system (Mullaperiyar dam -> diversion tunnel -> Vaigai dam)

entitled.basis: PWD release order: 51.09 cusecs (125 MLD) year-round continuous

received.note: The city draws roughly 900 of its 1,500 mcft allotment - operationally ~115 MLD via the two Vaigai lines against the 125 MLD entitlement

instrument.label: PWD letter Lr. No. DB/JD01/384/C.10(P)/2018, dt. 26 Dec 2018

arrangements.note: One of the few Indian city entitlements with the actual order number in the public record (via the ADB TNUFIP Tranche-2 IEE).

events.title: The Periyar lease - the ancestor instrument
events.note: The 999-year Periyar Lease Deed between Travancore and the Madras Presidency sent west-flowing Periyar water east through the ghats - the instrument beneath the Mullaperiyar dam, the diversion tunnel, and ultimately Madurai's tap. Still contested between Kerala and Tamil Nadu 140 years on.

futures.project: Mullai Periyar Lower Camp check dam + Pannaipatty WTP expansion (ADB TNUFIP Tranche 2)
futures.status: Design horizon 2034: new check dam, intake, 16.85 km raw-water main and +125 MLD treatment - effectively doubling the drinking draw on the same entitlement system

gaps: No public daily metering of the corporation's actual draw - the ~900 mcft figure is an annual aggregate from project documents; day-level receipts would need the utility's own records.
The PWD letter itself is cited in the ADB IEE but not published as a standalone document.
En-route entitlements (towns drawing from the same conveyance) are not publicly itemised, so Madurai's share cannot be placed within the full system ledger.
